Argument for “Engaged, Truly in Love, Forced Apart” (Our Position)

1. Larhgan’s Vows and Emotional Consistency  
  a. “Good-by…only from a distance”  
    • <invalid_quote>“This is, in effect, good-by,” she continued. “We shall see each other…only from a distance.”</invalid_quote> (p.2) shows permanent separation, not temporary ignorance.  
    • She surrenders her grimpatch: <invalid_quote>“you give me mine…you might want to give yours to some nice beggar girl.”</invalid_quote> (p.3) only because law and social order forbid betrothal, not because she doubts her love.  
  b. Exclusive Faithfulness  
    • <invalid_quote>“I promise you there will never be anyone else for me”—“I'm proud of you, Skkiru.”</invalid_quote> (pp.6,13) Repeated “fuzzed…eyes,” “soulful glances” show genuine affection and pride at his sacrifices.  
    • She adopts “religious life,” “feast days…kiss the hem of my robe,” “rain-dance…stop rain” as social rituals, acknowledging his role, not rejecting him permanently.

2. Skkiru’s Sacrifice and Hope of Reunion  
  a. Patriotism, Not Self-Advancement  
    • <invalid_quote>“I’ll speak broken…I’ll forsake my normal habits…and I’ll even beg. But I don’t have to like doing it.”</invalid_quote> (p.7) He loathes the role and only endures to “for Snaddra,” not to usurp Bbulas.  
    • He shows “melancholy pleasure” at processions, “nostalgia for warm underskirts” (pp.14–15) and “gentle, moody pleasure to envisage his own funeral,” indicating readiness to die rather than expose them. A true schemer would avoid self-destructive risk.  
  b. No Alternative Choice  
    • He contemplates emigration only to abandon “playing the game” and lose Larhgan (p.15). His “patriotic duty” binds him to the beggar role.  
    • Libel laws: <quote> didn't dare offer this conclusion aloud; the libel laws of  Snaddra were very severe. </quote> (p.5) Any exposure risks execution and ruin of the entire plan.

3. Lack of Genuine Secret Scheme  
  a. Improvisation, Not Coherent Plan  
    • Pontoons: “habit of collecting junk,” “while Bbulas was looking the other way” (p.52) only “to stave off doom”—takes time, risks detection, no guarantee of political power once Earthmen arrive.  
    • Chocolate: He consumes it immediately for survival (“increases resistance to weather”), not hoard as currency. A true agent would trade it later for political advantage.  
  b. Bbulas’ Control of Rituals and Narratives  
    • All social positions assigned by “impartial lot,” approved by Parliament and President (p.3), illustrate institutional control. Skkiru lacked authority to “organize this culture” (p.3); only Bbulas had “qualification to administer it.”  
    • Processions, huts, dances, costly clothing imported—managed by Bbulas—without Skkiru’s planning. If Skkiru were prime mover, he would have contributed “antique blueprints” himself rather than depend on Bbulas’ “rare tape-and-book dealer” purchases (p.15).

4. Textual Refutation of Debater_B’s “Unaware” Thesis  
  a. Recognition of Status Change  
    • She “mustn’t suspect…or we’re finished” implies that exposure kills credibility (p.12). Larhgan never questions Skkiru’s authenticity, because she sees his “genuine” suffering. If she recognized him, why would she not use her priestess influence to aid him?  
    • On “rain-dance,” both Bbulas and Larhgan invite him to “complete cooperation” (p.13). A true suitor hiding behind performance would not solicit his own participation as beggar after arrival of anthropologists.  
  b. Lack of “True Agency”  
    • Even after he “arrived” first at the ship (p.52), Larhgan reacts only with ritual words given by Bbulas, not personal greeting. If she recognized her fiancé, she would break protocol to comfort him, not preserve “primitive” façade.  
    • Raoul later notes “Why only the beggar wears mudshoes?” (p. 54), while Larhgan remains “erected” in priestly garb. If Skkiru planned to win her hand, he would abandon beggar garb immediately upon arrival to demonstrate superiority.

5. Genre and Character Consistency  
  a. Theme of Sacrificial Love  
    • The text emphasizes sacrifice: “heart will be breaking,” “wetter season,” lovers torn apart—a classic tragic romance, not lighthearted ruse.  
    • Snaddrath “library” and “fictapes” stressed emotional impoverishment: Larhgan “fuzzes” exploring Terran “emotion,” signifying her longing for genuine affection, not performance.  
  b. Skkiru’s “Quiver” of Doubt  
    • <quote> a tiny pang of doubt and  apprehension began to quiver in his seco</quote> (p.1) Genuine lover’s fear of permanent separation, not acting part.

Conclusion  
Only our interpretation—engaged lovers torn apart by planetary necessity, clinging to exclusive hope of reunion—fits the repeated emotional language, self-destructive sacrifices, and Larhgan’s vows of eternal fidelity. Debater_B’s “secret courtship” theory fails to account for: (1) libel and protocol risks; (2) immediate consumption of contraband; (3) lack of Larhgan’s personal recognition; (4) absence of any coherent plan to seize power until ruse ends in death or ruin. Our position explains every act as driven by love and duty, in accordance with the text.
